key_insight: On simulated wavefields, a PINN with exact boundary and initial constraints accurately identifies the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 without boundary or initial-condition penalty tuning.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a potential non-destructive alternative to dedicated resonance tests for characterizing shear coupling in PMUTs and surface acoustic wave devices.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state exactly.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse, noisy wavefield observations.
Non-dimensionalize governing coefficients to comparable scales near unity.
evidence_signal: The full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error on finite-element data at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB sweep; displacement-only training achieved 0.45% mean error on finite-element data.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-only; experimental performance and constructing exact constraint functions for complex device geometries remain untested.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
